title: Ocarina of Time Was Almost Set Entirely Inside One Castle
hook:
Miyamoto's first plan for Ocarina of Time kept the whole game inside one castle, and he even pitched playing it in first person. Today, November 5, the Switch 2 remake lands and you can hum the songs into the mic. Which song are you humming first?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Ocarina of Time was almost a game that never let you leave one castle? When work began, Shigeru Miyamoto thought a single building, Ganon's Castle, might be enough for the whole game. He has said that in the worst case, Link would never have gone outside. He also proposed playing it in first person, so you could take in the wide landscape. Link would only appear on screen when a fight broke out. Designer Yoshiaki Koizumi, who built Link's model, said he could not stand to see his Link not appear. Once the team added child Link, the hero had to be visible, and the first person idea was dropped. The game also started life as a disk game for the Sixty Four D D add on. Slow disk reads pushed it onto a cartridge instead. It finally shipped on the Nintendo 64 in November 1998. It earned Famitsu's first ever perfect forty out of forty, and it still holds a ninety nine on Metacritic. And today, November fifth, Nintendo's remade version launches on Switch Two. It has overhauled visuals, fully voiced cutscenes, a jump button, and you can hum Link's songs into the console's built in microphone. Which song are you humming first? Follow for more gaming history.
